question.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2}$ of two cans is drawn from a population. The population has cans of two different volumes, $0.5\,\text{L}$ and $\text{1}\,\text{L},$ distributed in the ratio $2:3.$ Calculate $\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}].$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}.
$$

We're told that the cans in the population have volumes $0.5\,\text{L}$ and $1\,\text{L},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $2:3.$ Therefore, to compute the population mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $2+3=5$ cans only with the following volumes:

$$
0.5\,\text{L},\,0.5\,\text{L},\,1\,\text{L},\,1\,\text{L},\,1\,\text{L}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2\cdot 0.5+3\cdot 1) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(1+3) \\  & =\frac{4}{5} \\  & =0.8\,\text{L},\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2\cdot {0.5}^{2}+3\cdot {1}^{2})-{0.8}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(3.5)-0.64 \\  & =0.7-0.64 \\  & =0.06\,{\text{L}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the sample size $n=2,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}=\frac{0.06}{2}=0.03\,{\text{L}}^{2}.
$$
